issues.description: Mismatch for Farm.singFarmSong() and its helper singFarmSongVerse(Animal): the problem statement UML (problem_statement.md line 20) declares singFarmSong():void and the textual instructions (problem_statement.md lines 112-117) say to implement singFarmSong() to print the song (i.e., a void printing method). The template (src/de/tum/cit/ase/Farm.java) defines public void singFarmSong() (line 9) and a helper private void singFarmSongVerse(/*Animal animal*/) (line 18) intended to print the verses. The solution (src/de/tum/cit/ase/Farm.java) defines public String singFarmSong() (line 59) and private String singFarmSongVerse(Animal) (line 33) and returns the song text. This divergence (void/printing vs String/returning) is a real inconsistency across artifacts that will confuse students about the expected API and may cause tests or example usage to fail depending on which convention is enforced.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the return types and behavior consistent across problem statement, template, and solution. Two viable options: (A) Prefer matching the UML/text which specify printing: change the solution so singFarmSong() is declared public void singFarmSong() and singFarmSongVerse(Animal) is void and performs printing (update implementation to print each verse). Update solution code and any tests that expect a String. (B) Or, if returning the full song text is desired, update the problem statement (text and UML) and the template to declare singFarmSong():String and singFarmSongVerse(...) : String and change the textual wording from “prints” to “returns the song text”; update tests accordingly. Document the chosen convention in the instructions and align the UML, template method signatures, and reference solution to that convention.
